name: NIST beam neutron lifetime experiment BL3
notes: The BL3 conceptual design report (2021) is cited by the BL2 paper as "unpublished" and was not used; the status rests on the collaboration's June 2025 conference abstract.
No lineage edge to BL2 is recorded because the sources describe BL3 only as an "entirely new apparatus" improving on the previous experiment.

physics_goals.quote: reduce the neutron lifetime uncertainty from the beam method to <0.3 s.
physics_goals.value: Reduce the beam-method neutron lifetime uncertainty to below 0.3 s and the systematic uncertainties to the 10^-4 level

summary.plain: The next-generation NIST neutron-lifetime experiment, under construction. It uses a larger magnet, proton trap and neutron beam to measure the lifetime to better than 0.3 seconds with the beam method and to test the method’s systematic effects.
summary.technical: BL3 beam neutron lifetime: entirely new apparatus with a larger magnet and proton trap, a larger neutron beam and a segmented silicon detector (a factor 100 in proton trapping rate), goal below 0.3 s on the beam-method lifetime and systematics at the 10^-4 level. Funded 2022; integration planned 2026; run at the NCNR.
